claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.harm: adds complexity and invites inconsistent naming between cmake targets, output names, and manpages
claims.quote: This change adds complexity and invites less consistent naming, and the PR description claims it is useful without explaining why it is useful.

settled_by.quote: Your logic makes sense even if I disagree, and if you think this approach is better, I've acked the code change and don't want to get in the way.

claims.author: 151henry151
claims.harm: generator expression resolves CONFIG/DEBUG postfixes, which would cause install failure if suffixed manpages do not exist in doc/man/
claims.quote: the genex also picks up <CONFIG>_POSTFIX / DEBUG_POSTFIX... doc/man/ won't have a postfixed page, so you get an install-time failure only in that config

notes: ryanofsky agreed to disagree on the drop-in target/output name divergence after hebasto explained the QML migration strategy. 151henry151's observation regarding DEBUG_POSTFIX is recorded as an open non-blocking claim per the doubt-preference rule, though it causes no issues in current master.

participants.note: asked whether bitcoin-qt is being renamed or staying named bitcoin-qt
concept -0 on diverging CMake target names and output names, but agreed to disagree
tested ACKed, but noted genex tracks DEBUG_POSTFIX which could cause install failure

support.author: ryanofsky
support.reason: the change does seem safe, just not clearly motivated

support.author: BrandonOdiwuor
support.reason: The change is correct and future-proofs manpage installation for targets using OUTPUT_NAME* / RUNTIME_OUTPUT_NAME* properties.

support.author: 151henry151
support.reason: Concept ACK as cheap future-proofing — $<TARGET_FILE_BASE_NAME> is the right tool here anyway (including that it drops the .exe suffix on Windows rather than making us hand-roll that)
